slides.title:
Your wedding
budget in
*10 steps*
slides.sub: Do them in this order and every decision after gets easier.

slides.title: Know your *numbers*
items: Look at the full picture: savings, income, family help
Set a total you can *comfortably* afford
Name your top priorities. Spend more there.

slides.title: Decide what *drives* cost
items: Pick a guest count early. It touches almost every line.
Fixed costs (venue, photographer) vs. changing costs (catering)

slides.title: Protect the *plan*
items: Track every payment, deposit and due date

slides.title:
Venue and catering
are usually the
*biggest* lines.
slides.body: Guest count moves catering. That's why step 4 comes so early.

slides.title:
*12 questions*
to ask before
you sign
slides.sub: The more you know up front, the smoother everything after.

slides.title: Can it *work?*
items: How many hours are included (setup to cleanup)?

slides.title: What are we *paying* for?
items: What's in the rental fee? Tables, chairs, linens?
Any decoration rules? (candles, string lights, florals)
Do you offer in-house catering? Tastings?
Can we bring our own caterer? Any fees?

slides.title: Will guests be *comfortable?*
items: Where can out-of-town guests stay nearby?
What's the backup plan for an outdoor ceremony?

slides.title: No *surprises*
items: What are the deposit and cancellation policies?

slides.title:
Build a timeline
that doesn't
*break*
slides.sub: One page. What happens, when, and who owns it.

slides.title: Start in the *middle*
items: Write your ceremony time in the middle
List hard stops: venue end, sunset, music curfew
Work backward: getting ready, vendors, photos, setup
Work forward: cocktails, dinner, toasts, send-off

slides.title: +15 minutes
slides.body:
when 5 or more people
must move together.

slides.title: +20 minutes
slides.body:
when a car, shuttle
or parking lot is involved.

slides.title: Family photos *multiply*
slides.body: Ask your photographer how long each group takes. Then multiply by your number of groups.

slides.title:
Your ceremony may
start a few
minutes *late.*
slides.body: Don't build a timeline that breaks if it does.

slides.title:
Build your
guest list
without the *drama*
slides.sub: 6 steps that balance people, budget and space.

slides.title:
Budget and
venue *first*
slides.body: How many fit? What can you spend per guest? Keep a buffer for surprises.

slides.title:
Your core
*people*
slides.body: Family, close friends, wedding party. The people you can't imagine the day without.

slides.title: A *two-tier* list
slides.body: Tier one: must invite. Tier two: invite as RSVPs come in, if space and budget allow.

slides.title:
Plus-ones and
kids: decide *early*
slides.body: Then say it clearly on your invitation or wedding website.

slides.title:
RSVP deadline:
*4–6 weeks* out
slides.body: Give travelers time. Follow up when it passes.

slides.title:
Plan for
*no-shows*
slides.body: Not everyone you invite will come. Use your final RSVPs to set catering and seating.
